doc.title: Jimmy Heath interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, September 8, 2014

title: Real Book royalties and Sher Music
summary: Heath says he gets nothing from the pirated Real Books but is paid by legitimate publishers such as Sher Music.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Do you get — you know let’s say a Jimmy Heath song, let’s say it showed up in the Real Book. Did you ever get any compensation for that?

Not for those gangsters who made those books. But as far as the legitimate books, you know, I get — Jamey Aebersold or something like that. Or the guy in California who put three or four of my songs in his book. I can’t think of his name. He makes big books about songs from the jazz world.
Right. And the Real Book has now been made legal sort of.
Yeah, well who is the publisher?
Yeah I get money from him for my songs. Danny Sher?
I’m not sure what his first name is.
